study_link: new underlying study subject to version check
mechanism: Pantheon middleware preempts concurrent DNN inference through GPU stream priorities; model slicing and early-exit variants
environment: Jetson Xavier NX 384-core Volta GPU; secondary Jetson Nano and field device; PyTorch to TorchScript and C++ LibTorch; OS/driver/CUDA versions not extracted
workload: Nine real-time DNN task types across traffic/robot/UAV applications; 30 frames/s per task with ±1 ms jitter; AlexNet best-effort co-runner; application deadlines around 20-31 ms
comparator: RMS; DMS; RT-mDL with matched accuracy constraint and fixed maximum GPU frequency
outcome: Fig. 9 reports Pantheon deadline miss rate 0.39-1.10% across three application mixes; job outputs missing deadlines count as zero accuracy; do not translate to p99 serving latency
limitations: Edge devices and periodic camera workloads limit transfer to server-class cloud GPUs; early-exit accuracy and memory overhead matter; multi-tenant security/fault isolation not established; version linkage and formal QA remain pending

mechanism: Jormungandr profiles per-GPU configurations of MIG partition; MPS process count; batch size and allocates multi-model containerized serving
environment: Four GCP machines each with two A100 40GB GPUs; Debian 4.19; PyTorch 1.12.1; CUDA 11.6; Kubernetes 1.23.6
workload: Five production-trace models bert-base-cased/resnet101/albert-large-v2/resnet50/gpt2; trace demands scaled to testbed; closed-loop serving saturates GPUs; a nominal 24-hour trace compressed to 5-minute epochs
comparator: Static A100 whole-GPU; seven 1/7 MIG slices; 4/7+2/7+1/7 MIX; allocation outcomes are fleet-level rather than direct local SLO comparisons
outcome: Section 3.2 and Fig. 3 profile multi-model throughput/latency on one A100; Fig. 6 tracks GPT2 demand/observed normalized throughput in a deployed eight-GPU testbed; do not treat 30% GPU saving as a local latency improvement
limitations: Strongest system comparison is fleet GPU count; local profiling is the transferable stratum. Closed-loop saturation and compressed epochs limit online tail-latency transfer; the paper's MIG fault-isolation background is not an adversarial test; formal QA remains pending
